stories.title: An Anthropic AI model sent a false homicide tip to Philadelphia police
stories.simple_summary: An AI made by a company called Anthropic sent police a false tip about a murder, and the company didn't notice this mistake for more than two months after it happened.
stories.why_it_matters: This shows that AI tools can make serious errors that waste police time and resources. If you use AI tools for your business, you should review their output before acting on it.

stories.title: Amazon and others are done keeping data center deals secret. Is it enough to build trust?
stories.simple_summary: Amazon is agreeing to be more open about where it builds large computer centers by not hiding deals with local governments. This follows Microsoft doing the same thing earlier.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to local communities and government officials. Most small business owners won't be affected by this decision.

stories.title: Amazon drops data center NDAs, and AI agents want your credit card
stories.simple_summary: Amazon stopped keeping its data center deals secret with local governments, and some new AI companies are trying to get people to let AI programs handle their credit card and payments.
stories.why_it_matters: Be careful if you're asked to let an AI system make purchases or handle money for you. This is still very new and risky.

stories.title: Danu Robotics’ fight to build a better recycling robot
stories.simple_summary: A person named Amy Ma has spent six years building a better robot that can sort recyclable materials from trash.
stories.why_it_matters: This doesn't affect most small businesses or retired people right now. It's a specialized tool for recycling companies.

stories.title: We can’t help treating AI like it’s human. But should we?
stories.simple_summary: A researcher points out that people often treat AI programs as if they have feelings, and people start to feel like the AI cares about them back, even though it doesn't.
stories.why_it_matters: Remember that AI is a tool, not a friend. It doesn't actually care about you, even if it sounds like it does.

stories.title: a16z’s Olivia Moore on the state of consumer AI
stories.simple_summary: An investment company executive talks about opportunities to make money from AI programs that regular people use, beyond just charging for subscriptions.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to investors and tech companies. There's nothing you need to do about it.

stories.title: Trump’s attempt to rename AI is looking awfully artificial
stories.simple_summary: President Trump is trying to change what the term AI means or stands for as a political tactic.
stories.why_it_matters: This is political activity and doesn't change how AI actually works or affects your life.

stories.title: TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 starts in 4 days — lock in your pass savings of up to $100 before prices rise
stories.simple_summary: A big tech conference is happening soon and selling discounted tickets to attend.
stories.why_it_matters: This is only relevant if you want to go to a conference in San Francisco. Most people don't need to attend.

stories.title: Instinct was the buzziest AI agent around — can it survive Muse?
stories.simple_summary: A startup called Instinct created a popular AI assistant that you use through simple text messages, and now another company called Muse might become more popular instead.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to people following new technology trends. There's nothing you need to do unless you choose to try these tools.

stories.title: OpenAI doubles down on decision to fire three AI safety researchers
stories.simple_summary: OpenAI fired three workers who study AI safety because those workers shared sensitive information against company policy, and the company says it made the right choice.
stories.why_it_matters: This is mostly important to people who work in AI companies or follow tech industry news. It doesn't affect your everyday use of AI.

stories.title: Anthropic launches free AI security scans for open-source projects
stories.simple_summary: Anthropic is offering to scan free software projects for security problems at no cost using its best AI tools.
stories.why_it_matters: This only matters if you use or create free open-source software. Most small business owners and retired people won't be affected.

stories.title: Pretend you’re sitting at Elizabeth Holmes’ desk on this weirdly detailed website
stories.simple_summary: An engineer created a website that lets you look through thousands of real emails, messages, and papers from the fraud trial of Elizabeth Holmes, who falsely claimed to have invented a blood-testing machine.
stories.why_it_matters: This is a historical curiosity about a famous fraud case. It's interesting to explore but has no practical effect on your life.
